summary: Iter181 Price Manager follow-up #2 tested end-to-end — all 4 new features work. Backend: 5/5 pytest cases pass (unconfigured city returns configured=false with empty prices/ratecards + populated templates; apply-across with include=['services','ratecards','fees'] propagates fees to targets; without 'fees' target fees are preserved; services+ratecards still enables the category on target). Frontend verified against Bakhri (unconfigured service area): (1) pm-new-city banner shown + pm-unsaved dirty state auto-set + Rate Card tab inputs pre-filled from category template (e.g. AC Split: 549 / 699 / … 6/6 filled). (2) pm-rc-preview opens customer-style RateCardModal titled 'AC Repair & Service · Bakhri' with AzoCover brand chip + groups. (3) pm-rc-bulk-pct=10 + pm-rc-bulk-apply scaled first row 549 → 604, kept Unsaved banner. (4) pm-rc-apply-across dialog shows all 3 scopes (services, ratecards, fees); confirm enabled after selecting Ranchi + fees scope. Regression: pm-rc-category switches card (AC → Electrician), pm-rc-use-template present. Saving Bakhri succeeded (toast 'Pricing updated for Bakhri'), pm-new-city cleared, pm-unsaved cleared.

issues: After saving an auto-inherited (brand-new) service area, the city still shows '0 / 16 priced' in the service-area chip because service prices are not auto-inherited (only rate-card overrides are, per spec). Behaviour matches the specification but is a potential user-confusion point — consider a hint telling the admin to also set service prices.

critical_code_review_comments: apply_across now correctly honours 'fees' scope: `fees = src.fees if 'fees' in inc else target_doc.fees` — target fees preserved when not included (verified by regression test).
PriceManager.load(): auto-inherit builds the seeded ratecards map from category templates for unconfigured cities, which flips `summary.rc` dirty and surfaces Save. Clean, minimal change.
RateCardPrices.applyPct(): correctly falls back to template default when the city override is empty (`raw = ov[k] || r[k]`). Rounding uses Math.round so 549×1.10=603.9 → 604 (shown).
buildCityCard() filters rows with empty service_charge and drops empty groups — matches the public apply_ratecard contract. Preview is read-only (no cart props passed).
